verdicts.one_line: The most self-aware reconciliation in the document set, but it cannot be trusted as-is because AI-generated tags enter the Labs path as human_capture and the 'only tag leaves the device' claim contradicts cloud-side visual judging.
verdicts.strongest_part: The honesty discipline: committed docs win, FrugalRoute is flagged as unvetted, the discard problem is treated as load-bearing, and System B is explicitly walled off from Labs with a grep-verifiable no-import rule.
verdicts.weakest_part: System A's own tag path uses a local LLM and M3 to generate tags that are then labeled human_capture and shared to Labs/IPFS — the document polices the System B fence while leaving AI inside the Labs corral; additionally, the diagram says only text leaves the device while M3 is supposed to judge uncertain frames visually.
verdicts.provenance_leakage_risk: high - System A's AI-generated tags are explicitly categorized as human_capture and pushed into the Labs/IPFS path; System B separation does not address AI inside the capture→tag→share flow, and shared model/runtime/training artifacts create further leakage vectors.
verdicts.discard_mitigations_verdict: insufficient - the four consensus mitigations are necessary but not sufficient; missing a fifth mitigation for adversarial/novelty 'quiet-but-pivotal' inputs, a closed loop where M3 audit results actually change thresholds, a statistically powered audit sample, and a human-feedback channel for corrected misses.

answers_to_OQs.OQ-1: FrugalRoute is not a recognizable maintained project in public knowledge; FrugalGPT is the 2023 research/pattern reference (Luo et al.). Do not make it a dependency; implement the ~50-line confidence router plus semantic cache yourself, and if a library is desired evaluate RouteLLM or LiteLLM routing instead.
answers_to_OQs.OQ-2: No, the separation is not clean enough. System A stores AI-written tags as human_capture, so AI output rides the Labs path by design. System B also shares the same Mac Studio/Ollama runtime, so 'no import path' only proves code-level separation. Required: (a) a precise provenance class for AI-annotated human capture or a human-confirmation gate before Labs eligibility; (b) separate model instances, namespaces, queues, and egress rules for A and B; (c) a rule that no model fine-tuned on Labs data can be used by System B or shared.
answers_to_OQs.OQ-3: The 0.70/0.85 split is directionally correct but 0.70 auto-approve on a 1-3B mobile model is too low and assumes confidence calibration that these models usually lack. Split decisions: discard, tag, and share should have separate thresholds; calibrate with human-labeled samples and conformal/evidential uncertainty; add drift monitoring. 0.85 for M3 is reasonable.
answers_to_OQs.OQ-4: No, the four mitigations are not sufficient as the sole defense. They cover random and temporal loss but not adversarial or 'visually quiet yet pivotal' inputs. Add a fifth mitigation: anomaly/novelty scoring plus mandatory human review of flagged near-misses, and make the M3 discard audit trigger threshold changes, not just a report.
answers_to_OQs.OQ-5: Mostly honest, but 'routine' modules (CLI, utilities, docs) can become load-bearing and security-relevant over time. Add promotion criteria, periodic DeepSeek re-review of previously 'routine' modules, and keep cloud review mandatory for anything touching auth, filesystem, networking, PII, or provenance.
answers_to_OQs.OQ-6: Anchoring bias is real and likely: the cloud receives the local draft first and will tend to repair rather than reframe it. Mitigate by generating an independent cloud draft without seeing the local one, or by running a fork experiment (draft-assisted vs draft-agnostic) over a sprint before trusting the pattern.
answers_to_OQs.OQ-7: Not believable as stated. $1.44/day and 99.5% local require explicit frame volume, M3 pricing, calibration-audit sample size, temporal-floor overhead, and battery/thermal assumptions. The calibration sample alone can add several percent cloud calls. Provide a transparent cost model with a hard budget alert.

issues.problem: Tags are generated by the local LLM / M3 and then classified as human_capture and pushed into Labs/IPFS. On its face this violates invariant #4 ('AI forbidden in Labs'). The document only polices System B while leaving AI inside System A's Labs path.
issues.fix: Define human_capture precisely. Either (a) require human confirmation before AI-written tags become Labs-eligible, (b) introduce a separate ai_assisted_meta provenance class that cannot be presented as pure human_capture, or (c) explicitly amend invariant #4 with community approval.

issues.problem: 'Only the tag leaves the device' contradicts L3 M3 judging uncertain frames and the periodic M3 discard audit; M3 is a vision model and cannot judge visual content from text tags alone.
issues.fix: Specify exactly what is sent to L3 for escalation and audit: blurred frames, embeddings, or compact local descriptors — and state retention, deletion, and PII policy for those artifacts.

issues.problem: L5 'system adapts / model improves' implies training on Labs-eligible human_capture signal. The resulting model weights are opaque artifacts that could carry Labs data into System B or other nodes, creating a second-order provenance leak.
issues.fix: Forbid training on Labs data unless the invariant is formally changed; otherwise keep any such learned model strictly ai_generated, record weight provenance, and never allow it into the Labs or System B shared inference path.

issues.problem: 0.70 auto-approve is too low for a 1-3B model that is typically miscalibrated, especially when auto-approve can lead to IPFS sharing. Confidence is not probability of correctness.
issues.fix: Calibrate on-device with held-out human-labeled samples; use separate thresholds for discard, tag, and share; use conformal prediction or evidential uncertainty; monitor calibration drift over time.

issues.problem: The four mitigations lack adversarial/novelty detection and a closed feedback loop; periodic audit reporting does not by itself correct the threshold.
issues.fix: Add a fifth mitigation: anomaly/novelty scoring with mandatory human review of near-misses, and make audit findings automatically trigger threshold/config changes with an audit log.

issues.problem: System A and System B share the same Mac Studio, Ollama instance, and local model. 'No import path' is only a compile-time/static guarantee; runtime data leakage is still possible through shared processes, logs, caches, or vector stores.
issues.fix: Run System A and System B in separate containers/model instances with separate API keys, queues, storage namespaces, and network egress rules; add a runtime test that B cannot read A's storage or logs.

issues.problem: '$1.44/day, 99.5% local' is asserted without a model and omits the calibration-sample overhead, temporal-floor retention, M3 audit costs, and phone battery/thermal constraints.
issues.fix: Publish a phase-by-phase cost model with assumptions: frames/day, cloud call percentage, per-call M3/DeepSeek pricing, audit sample %, and a hard budget alert.

issues.problem: G0 is marked done with n=1 and 80% consistency; a single-subject sample is not a statistically meaningful foundation for Phase 2 capture decisions.
issues.fix: Treat G0 as a pilot, expand to multiple participants before relying on it as a gate, and report confidence intervals rather than a single percentage.

issues.problem: Routine modules (CLI, utilities, docs) reviewed only by local Qwen can later become load-bearing or security-sensitive without being re-reviewed.
issues.fix: Add a promotion path, periodic DeepSeek re-review of previously routine modules, and mandatory cloud review for anything touching auth, filesystem, networking, or provenance.

issues.problem: Even presenting FrugalRoute as an open question gives it more status than it deserves; the repo has zero references to it and it is not a recognized tool.
issues.fix: Remove the name from the architecture entirely, implement the internal router, and only reconsider a named dependency after an explicit evaluation with criteria.

missing_considerations: PII can leak through text tags even after visual blur — names, locations, and relationships in descriptions need their own tag-level PII filter.
Battery/thermal feasibility of continuous on-device 1-3B inference on glasses+phone has not been analyzed.
Only-tag-leaves-device vs cloud visual judging is an unresolved contradiction that affects privacy, cost, and architecture.
L5 learning from Labs data creates model-weight provenance leakage that the document does not address.
AI-tag homogenization risk: IPFS convergence of AI-generated tags may erode genuine human diversity of perspective — the network could converge toward model priors, not human signal.
Consent/legal considerations for bystander capture are absent.
Prompt-injection from a codebase could exfiltrate private code through System B's cloud escalation; System B needs its own egress review.
Threshold configuration needs versioning, drift alerts, and an immutable audit log, not just 'recorded changes'.
Offline-mode behavior for glasses/phone and IPFS sync failure handling is unspecified.
M3 discard audit and escalation are both cloud calls; the claimed 5-10% cloud budget must include the audit sample, otherwise the cost model is understated.
